<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par50 />{{GHGpar-heading|50|The Participle}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|a}}
'''1.''' Qal has both an active participle, called {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}} from its form ({{GHGheb|text=פֹּעֵל}}), and a passive, ''Pāʿûl'' ({{GHGheb|text=פָּעוּל}}).<ref>The constr. st. {{GHGheb|text=נְאֻם}} in the formula {{GHGheb|text=נאם יהוה}}, ''the word'' (properly the ''whispering'') ''of the Lord'', &c., is always written defectively.</ref>

''Pāʿûl'' is generally regarded as a survival of a passive of Qal, which still exists throughout in Arabic, but has been lost in Hebrew (see, however, {{GHGpar|52|e}}), just as in Aramaic the passives of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} are lost, except in the participles. But instances of the form ''quṭṭāl'' are better regarded as remnants of the passive participle Qal (see {{GHGpar|52|s}}), so that {{GHGheb|text=פָּעוּל}} must be considered as an original verbal noun; cf. Barth, {{GHGcite|title=Nominalbildung}}, p. 173 ff.

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|b}}
'''2.''' In the intransitive verbs ''mid. e'' and ''mid. o'', the form of the participle active of Qal coincides in form with the 3rd sing. of the perfect, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁן|translate=sleeping}}, from {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁן}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָגוֹר}} (only orthographically different from the perf. {{GHGheb|text=יָגֹר}}) ''fearing''; cf. the formation of the participle in {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, {{GHGpar|51|a}}. On the other hand, the participle of verbs ''mid. a'' takes the form {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֵל}} (so even from the ''transitive'' {{GHGheb|text=שָׂנֵא|translate=to hate}}, part. {{GHGheb|text=שׂנֵא}}). The ''ô'' of these forms has arisen through an obscuring of the ''â'', and is therefore unchangeable, cf. {{GHGpar|9|q}}. The form {{GHGheb|text=קָטָל}} (with a changeable {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} in both syllables), which would correspond to the forms {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁן}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָגֹר}}, is only in use as a noun, cf. {{GHGpar|84|f|a}}. The formation of the participle in {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, and ''Hithpaʿēl'' follows a different method.

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|c}}
'''3.''' Participles form their feminine ({{GHGheb|text=קֹֽטְלָה}} or {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֶ֫לֶת}}) and their plural like other nouns ({{GHGpar|80|e}}, {{GHGpar|84|r|a}}, {{GHGpar|84|s|a|nonumber=1}}, {{GHGpar|94}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|d}}
Rem. 1. From the above it follows, that the ''ā'' of the form {{GHGheb|text=יָשֵׁן}} is lengthened from ''ă'', and consequently changeable (e.g. {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=יְשֵׁנָה}}); and that the ''ô'' of {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֵל}} on the other hand is obscured from an unchangeable ''â''.<ref>Cf. Vollers, ‘''Das Qâtil-partizipium'',’ in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZA.|Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und verwandte Gebiete, ed. by C. Bezold. Lpz. 18S6 ff.}}}} 1903, p. 312 ff.</ref> In Arabic the verbal adjective of the form ''qătĭl'' corresponds to the form ''qāṭēl'', and the part. ''qâtĭl'' to ''qôṭēl''. In both cases, therefore, the ''ē'' of the second syllable is lengthened from ''ĭ'', and is consequently changeable (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קֹטֵל}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=קֹֽטְלִים}}; {{GHGheb|text=כָּבֵד}}, constr. pl. {{GHGheb|text=כִּבְדֵי}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|e}}
{{GHGheb|text=תּוֹמִיךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=5}}, instead of the form ''qôṭēl'', is an anomaly; it is possible, however, that {{GHGheb|text=תּוֹמֵיךְ}} (incorrectly written fully) is intended (cf. {{GHGheb|text=סֹבֵיב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=21}}), or even the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} of {{GHGheb|text=יָמַךְ}}. The form {{GHGheb|text=יֹסִף}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=38|verse=5|hidebook=1}} appears to stand for {{GHGheb|text=יֹסֵף}}, but most probably the Masora here (as certainly in {{GHGheb|text=יוֹסִיף}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=18}}) intends the 3rd sing. imperf. Hiph., for which the better form would be {{GHGheb|text=יוֹסֵף}}; {{GHGheb|text=אוֹבִיל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=27|verse=30}}, being a proper name and a foreign word, need not be considered.—{{GHGheb|text=אֹבַד}} (constr. state of {{GHGheb|text=אֹבֵד}}), with ''ă'' in the second syllable, occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=28}} (cf. moreover, {{GHGpar|65|d}}). On {{GHGheb|text=ה֫וֹלֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=7}} (for {{GHGheb|text=הוֹלֵם}}), see {{GHGpar|29|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|50|f}}
2. A form like the pass. ptcp. ''Pāʿûl'', but not to be confused with it, is sometimes found from ''intransitive verbs'', to denote an inherent quality, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָמוּן|translate=faithful}}; {{GHGheb|text=אָנוּשׁ|translate=desperate}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=15|verse=18}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=בָּטוּחַ|translate=trustful}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=112|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָצוּם|translate=strong}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁכוּר|translate=drunken}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=51|verse=21}}; and even from transitive verbs, {{GHGheb|text=אָחוּז|translate=handling}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=זָכוּר|translate=mindful}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָדוּעָ|translate=knowing}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=3}}; cf. {{GHGpar|84|m|a}}.<section end=par50 /><noinclude>
